tier_reason: README shows a BenchmarkDotNet table (Tlsf 82.27 us vs Libc 105.34 us, ratio 0.78) with .NET SDK 8.0.300 / RyuJIT DefaultJob and AMD Ryzen 9 7950X stated; benchmark code is public at src/XenoAtom.Allocators.Bench/BenchAllocator.cs.

corrections.caveats: C# library, not C++. Tiny benchmark: 2048 allocations from 7 fixed sizes (64, 96, 150, 200, 400, 1024, 4096) then frees. The 'Libc' baseline calls NativeMemory.AlignedAlloc(size, 64), which is _aligned_malloc on Windows MSVC CRT, not plain malloc. The TLSF side returns TlsfAllocationToken offsets into 64 KiB chunks from a managed chunk allocator (an offset/sub-allocator design), so the two sides do not do identical work. Windows only, single run.

notes: Opened BenchAllocator.cs: baseline is aligned CRT alloc, not malloc; that caveat is worth carrying. Metadata checked on github.com: 55 stars, BSD-2-Clause, last commit 2026-02-23 ('Fix benchmarks'). Language C# is outside the C++ focus.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed IEEE Computer Architecture Letters 2025 paper ('Old is Gold: Optimizing Single-Threaded Applications With ExGen-Malloc') comparing against dlmalloc and mimalloc on SPEC CPU2017; the PDF hosts (arXiv 2510.10219, ut-sysml.ece.utexas.edu, IEEE) are egress-blocked, so the numbers come from search snippets only and no code was found.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Geometric mean 1.19x over dlmalloc and 1.03x over mimalloc on SPEC CPU2017; 6.2%, 0.1% and 25.2% memory savings over mimalloc on SPEC CPU2017, redis-benchmark and mimalloc-bench (search snippet). The 1.93x-over-dlmalloc mimalloc-bench figure was not seen.
corrections.caveats: IEEE CAL 2025 short paper; arXiv (2510.10219), the UT Austin PDF and IEEE page are blocked, so numbers come from search snippets only. Snippets disagree with the original record (1.19x vs 1.17x over dlmalloc, 1.03x vs 1.05x over mimalloc). No repository found; single-threaded only.

notes: Corrected speedups to the abstract snippet wording (1.19x dlmalloc, 1.03x mimalloc). A paper-access retier could check compiler/CPU and a code release.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed USENIX ATC 2023 paper (cited in the repo README) reports up to 88% (4 KiB) and 98% (2 MiB) lower concurrent allocation time than the Linux frame allocator; benchmark scripts are public (luhsra/llfree-bench, luhsra/linux-alloc-bench), but the usenix.org PDF is blocked so CPU model and compiler could not be checked for A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Reduces allocation time for concurrent 4 KiB allocations by up to 88% and for 2 MiB allocations by up to 98% versus the Linux frame (buddy) allocator (USENIX ATC 2023 abstract, per search snippet). The 64% fewer compaction page movements figure was not seen.
corrections.caveats: Page-frame allocator, a different class from malloc. This repo is the C reimplementation; the ATC 2023 paper evaluated the Rust llfree-rs version inside a modified Linux (llfree-linux). Paper PDF on usenix.org blocked, numbers from search snippet; benchmark scripts in luhsra/llfree-bench and luhsra/linux-alloc-bench need a custom kernel build.

notes: Metadata from github.com: 12 stars, MIT, last commit 2026-09-17. Paper numbers confirmed only via snippet; the 64% compaction figure is unverified.
